raw:
Professor Windwhisper looks up from her folder.

“How is a student in the human seat meant to learn its practical duties?” you ask.

“A necessary question, Mr. Garvey.” Her voice is quiet enough that the room stills to hear it. “In an ordinary year, a Conclave heir arrives with tutors, family records, and a predecessor whose work can be observed. You have none of those advantages.”

Rashid shifts slightly in his chair.

Windwhisper continues. “You are a Conclave student, not yet a sitting Council delegate. This term will give you Council procedure, treaty interpretation, negotiation exercises, committee memoranda, and supervised study of prior proceedings. Professor Stone will oversee the surviving human historical material available to students.”

Caelindra taps one finger against her notes. “Available is doing a great deal of work there.”

“It usually does,” Windwhisper says. “Restricted histories require the Chancellor’s signature, regardless of the student requesting them.”

She turns a page.

“The human seat’s former functions have been divided provisionally among existing offices and committees. You will receive a current list of those functions, their holders, and the legal basis for each arrangement by noon. You should learn not only what the seat once did, but what others have done in its absence.”

“Will he receive the reports sent to it?” Rashid asks. “Or only the account prepared after someone decides what he needs to know?”

“Procedural reports relevant to his course work, yes,” says Windwhisper. “Private Council correspondence, no. The same boundary applies to every student here.”

“That seems reasonable,” Ashara says. “He needs to know where authority is actually being exercised, not be handed a ceremonial history and told he is prepared.”

Ysolde looks toward the framed Accords. “Some duties can be returned. Others will need to be negotiated again.”

Thessaly rests her hands on the table. “And whoever has held them may believe they have terms.”

Aldric’s posture grows a little straighter. “The Council has procedures for resolving that.”

Rashid glances at him. “Procedures are not the same as willingness.”

Before the exchange can sharpen, Seraphel speaks softly.

“An office absent still shapes each choice and voice;  
Learn where its silence borrows someone’s voice.”

Windwhisper inclines her head, accepting the point without comment.

“Precisely. Mr. Garvey, your practical education will include learning where the human seat’s absence has become convenient, necessary, or contested. The Academy can teach you the structure. Judgment will require more than a primer.”

She closes the folder.

“Now: residence expectations. Garvey House is shared Conclave housing. Its history does not grant any resident authority over another resident’s room, correspondence, or private affairs.”

The orientation moves on, but the promised list now has a place in the morning ahead of you.
